channel.title: The Catholic Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Review (catholicreview.org)

item.title: Getting to know our sacred space
item.description: Each of the objects, the surroundings in our Catholic churches, has a purpose and a history. Here is an overview of some of those sacred areas, objects and surroundings.

item.title: Affording Catholic schools: School choice programs, other options can help numbers add up
item.description: In a nation fixated on affordability, a Catholic school K-12 education can easily become a contested line in the family budget.

item.title: Trump administration asks federal court to pause Louisiana’s abortion pill challenge
item.description: A key national pro-life group has accused the U.S. Department of Justice of undermining Louisiana's efforts to roll back the Biden administration's eased restrictions on mifepristone when it asked a court to pause the Pelican State's challenge to that policy.

item.title: First woman to lead Church of England in its 1,400-year history confirmed in ceremony
item.description: Archbishop Sarah Mullally was confirmed as the 106th archbishop of Canterbury and the Church of England's first woman leader in its 1,400-year history.

item.title: Lack of faith, especially among youth, should spur evangelization, pope says
item.description: The increasing number of people who do not see the Gospel as a fundamental resource for their life should inspire -- not discourage -- Catholics in rediscovering the joy of evangelization, Pope Leo XIV said.

item.title: Deadly violence in Minneapolis tied to ICE agents is ‘unacceptable,’ top cardinal says
item.description: Asked about the deadly shootings by U.S. federal agents in Minneapolis, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, Vatican secretary of state, said the violence unfolding there is "unacceptable."

item.title: South Sudan bishops warn of genocide, plead for peace as fears of a full-scale war grow
item.description: As fears of a return to full-scale war in South Sudan escalate, Catholic bishops in the country have reiterated their call for peace and dialogue, amid fighting and mobilization in parts of the country.

item.title: Science teacher honors Challenger crew’s memory by encouraging curiosity, resilience, faith
item.description: A Houston-area Catholic school science teacher said the Challenger disaster remains one of the most defining moments of her early understanding of science and human exploration, shaping both her worldview and her vocation as an educator.

item.title: Sister Sigrid Simlik, former teacher in Baltimore, dies at 97
item.description: A funeral Mass will be offered Feb. 12 in Wisconsin for Dominican Sister of Sinsinawa Sigrid Simlik, who died Jan. 23. Sister Sigrid, a former teacher at St. Rose of Lima School in Brookland, was 97.

item.title: Noem unlawfully ended Venezuelan, Haitian deportation protections, says appeals court
item.description: A federal appeals court ruled late Jan. 28 that the Trump administration acted illegally when it ended legal protections for hundreds of thousands of people from Venezuela and Haiti, both predominantly Catholic countries, to remain in the United States without risk of deportation due to dangerous conditions in their respective homelands.
